title: HarvestLink
problem_statement: Independent restaurants and food co-ops spend 4-6 hours per week manually sourcing fresh produce from local farms via phone calls and fragmented email threads because no digital marketplace aggregates availability, pricing, and ordering for small farms within a 150-mile radius. Small and mid-size local farms lose 15-25% of harvestable produce to waste annually because they lack reliable demand signals until the week of harvest, forcing costly over-growing as insurance. Farm-to-table restaurants cannot plan menus more than 48 hours in advance due to informal, inconsistent farm availability updates. The convergence of post-pandemic local-food demand, farm financial fragility, and restaurateur margin pressure makes a structured B2B procurement solution urgently valuable now.
target_users: Independent restaurant owner-operator sourcing locally and managing menus week-to-week
Farm-to-table head chef planning seasonal menus with locally sourced ingredients
Small-to-mid-size local farm operator managing weekly harvest inventory and sales channels
Food co-op purchasing manager coordinating bulk produce orders for member households
Multi-location independent restaurant group buyer consolidating produce orders across locations
user_stories: As an independent restaurant owner-operator sourcing locally and managing menus week-to-week, I want to view a consolidated feed of available produce from farms within 150 miles with current prices and estimated harvest dates so that I can reduce sourcing time from 4-6 hours to under 30 minutes per week

As a farm-to-table head chef planning seasonal menus with locally sourced ingredients, I want 7-day forward visibility into farm inventory availability so that I can design and publish menus at least 5 days in advance rather than only 48 hours out

As a small-to-mid-size local farm operator managing weekly harvest inventory and sales channels, I want to post weekly available inventory with quantities, prices, and harvest dates so that I receive confirmed buyer commitments early enough to plant and harvest to actual demand and reduce produce waste by at least 15%

As a food co-op purchasing manager coordinating bulk produce orders for member households, I want to place standing weekly orders with automatic quantity adjustments based on farm availability so that I can guarantee consistent supply to members without manual renegotiation each week

As a multi-location independent restaurant group buyer consolidating produce orders across locations, I want to aggregate produce orders from all locations into a single cart and split delivery routing by location so that I eliminate duplicate vendor communications and reduce per-unit procurement costs

As a small-to-mid-size local farm operator managing weekly harvest inventory and sales channels, I want automated demand-signal alerts when buyer interest in a specific crop exceeds my listed quantity so that I can make informed planting and harvesting decisions 2-3 weeks ahead of harvest

As an independent restaurant owner-operator sourcing locally and managing menus week-to-week, I want to receive push notifications when a preferred farm lists a new product matching my saved ingredient preferences so that I can act on limited-availability items before they sell out
acceptance_criteria: Farm operators can create a weekly inventory listing including crop name, variety, quantity available, unit of measure, price per unit, harvest date, and pickup or delivery options in 5 or fewer steps and under 3 minutes
Buyers can search and filter available inventory by crop type, farm name, distance radius (up to 150 miles), price range, and harvest date window with results returning in under 2 seconds
7-day forward inventory visibility is displayed to buyers for every listed item, showing projected availability by day with a confidence indicator set by the farm

Buyers can place a one-time order or configure a standing weekly order with defined quantity, frequency, and auto-cancel threshold; standing orders require no manual reconfirmation unless farm availability drops below the threshold
Order confirmation is sent to both farm and buyer within 60 seconds of order placement, including itemized quantities, agreed price, delivery or pickup schedule, and contact details
Delivery routing tool generates an optimized multi-stop route for farms or third-party drivers fulfilling orders to multiple buyers on the same day, accepting up to 10 stops per route
A farm dashboard displays real-time sold vs. available quantity per SKU and cumulative weekly revenue, updating within 5 minutes of each new order

Buyers receive an in-app notification and email when a farm updates availability on a saved product or when a standing order cannot be fulfilled due to insufficient harvest, at least 72 hours before scheduled delivery
Platform enforces a minimum order value configurable by each farm (default $50) and rejects checkout if the cart falls below that threshold with a clear inline error message

All financial transactions are processed through the platform with funds held in escrow and released to the farm within 48 hours of confirmed delivery or pickup, with dispute initiation available for 24 hours post-delivery

success_metrics.metric: Weekly sourcing time per buyer (hours spent on phone, email, and manual coordination)
success_metrics.target: Under 1 hour per week per buyer within 90 days of activation

success_metrics.metric: Farm produce waste rate (percentage of harvestable inventory not sold)
success_metrics.baseline: 15-25% of harvestable produce wasted per farm
success_metrics.target: Under 10% waste rate per active farm within one full growing season (approximately 6 months)

success_metrics.metric: Menu planning lead time for farm-to-table restaurant buyers
success_metrics.target: At least 5 days in advance for 70% of weekly menus within 60 days of activation

success_metrics.metric: Gross merchandise value (GMV) processed through the platform monthly
success_metrics.target: $250,000 GMV per month by end of month 6 and $1,000,000 GMV per month by end of month 12

success_metrics.metric: Buyer order repeat rate (percentage of buyers placing orders in 2 consecutive weeks)
success_metrics.target: 60% week-over-week repeat order rate among buyers active for more than 30 days

success_metrics.metric: Farm inventory listing completion rate (farms that listed inventory at least once in the prior 7 days divided by total active farm accounts)
success_metrics.target: 75% of onboarded farms posting at least one inventory update per week within 60 days of farm onboarding

risks_open_questions: Cold-chain and last-mile delivery: HarvestLink does not own logistics infrastructure; will the platform integrate with third-party refrigerated delivery providers, or will farms and buyers self-arrange pickup, and how will delivery reliability and product quality in transit be guaranteed?

Farm technology adoption: Many small farm operators have limited smartphone or internet access and minimal comfort with software; what onboarding support, offline fallback mechanisms, or SMS-based listing flows are needed to reach sufficient farm-side supply density?

Demand signal reliability: If buyer demand forecasts on the platform are inaccurate (e.g., restaurants cancel orders last-minute), farms may still over- or under-harvest; what cancellation policy and financial penalties balance buyer flexibility against farm planning needs?

Geographic supply density: The marketplace requires simultaneous critical mass of farms and buyers within each 150-mile radius cluster; what is the minimum viable density (farms and buyers per region) and what is the sequenced launch market strategy?

Pricing transparency tension: Displaying real-time prices from competing farms may trigger a race-to-the-bottom on price that harms small farm viability; should the platform implement price floors, hide competitor pricing, or surface value attributes beyond price?

Regulatory and food safety compliance: B2B food transactions may require specific labeling, traceability documentation, or state-level agricultural broker licenses depending on jurisdiction; which compliance requirements apply in launch markets and who is responsible for ensuring them?

Payment terms mismatch: Restaurants typically expect net-30 payment terms with vendors while farms need cash flow within days of delivery; how will the platform structure payment timing and who absorbs the working capital gap?

Seasonal supply volatility: Produce availability is inherently seasonal and weather-dependent, making 7-day forward visibility inherently uncertain; how will confidence intervals be communicated to buyers and what SLA applies when farm availability falls short of commitments?
out_of_scope: Business-to-consumer (B2C) sales directly from farms to individual household shoppers
Retail grocery chains, large food distributors, or any buyer with more than 10 locations
Platform-owned or platform-operated delivery vehicles or cold-chain logistics infrastructure
Livestock, dairy, eggs, meat, or any non-produce agricultural product categories at launch
Financial lending, invoice factoring, or working capital products for farm operators
Crop planning software, soil management tools, or any farm operations management features beyond inventory listing
International farms or buyers outside the continental United States
Private-label or white-label product offerings sourced through the marketplace
Nutrition labeling, recipe generation, or consumer-facing menu publishing tools for restaurants
Sustainability certifications, carbon tracking, or ESG reporting features
